claims.location: source name, comment[label], characteristics[organism], organism part, material type, sex, and developmental stage: 80 Ref-set1 through Ref-set4 rows
claims.value: set-specific TMT126 reference identity; not applicable organism; all other listed biological properties not available
claims.evidence: The deposited labeling table supports only the set-specific Ref identity at TMT126 and its run/fraction coordinates. It does not define the reference material's biological composition, so contract-allowed reserved values replace cohort-level assertions.
The supplementary LC-MS/MS method names the instrument and top-speed precursor selection workflow; PRIDE registers the same instrument.
The supplementary method states that precursors were fragmented by CID at 30% for MS2, followed by SPS-MS3 HCD at 55%.

claims.location: comment[cleavage agent details], tolerances, and modification parameters
claims.value: Trypsin; 5 ppm; 0.6 Da; fixed Methylthio(C), variable Oxidation(M), fixed TMTpro(K and peptide N-terminus)
claims.evidence: The supplementary methods, PRIDE protocol, and deposited Proteome Discoverer settings agree on these preparation and search parameters.

limitations: No deposited crosswalk links the K/B source codes to the publication's Woman 1-44 clinical table; clinical and longitudinal factors are intentionally omitted.

TMT126 is described only as Ref. Its source name, reporter label, set, fraction, and RAW-file coordinates are retained, while organism is `not applicable` and organism part, material type, sex, developmental stage, and pooling status are `not available` because physical composition is undocumented.
Age, HIV status, HPV status/type, cytology, disease group, ancestry, and individual identity are not available at source-code resolution.
The single dissociation field records MS2 CID; MS3 HCD is documented in evidence but not representable simultaneously in that field.
A fresh-context adversarial review was unavailable, and review-gate state was not written because this campaign forbids git-state changes.
